flashcards.q: Quote SR 11-7's definition of a model and its two risk sources.
flashcards.a: 'A quantitative method, system, or approach that applies statistical, economic, financial, or mathematical theories, techniques, and assumptions to process input data into quantitative estimates.' Risk sources: model ERROR (design/data/implementation) and model MISUSE (outside approved scope). Issued April 2011 with OCC 2011-12.

flashcards.q: Name the three SR 11-7 validation components and one failure each catches.
flashcards.a: Conceptual soundness (wrong functional form/assumptions), outcomes analysis (calibration failure: predicted 2% defaults vs 8% realized), ongoing monitoring (decay after approval: PSI creep, drift). All three required or validation is incomplete.

flashcards.q: What three things make challenge 'effective' per SR 11-7?
flashcards.a: Authority (validators can block/restrict approval), incentives (compensation independent of business throughput), competence (quant skills to genuinely challenge). Reporting lines alone don't create independence.

flashcards.q: London Whale 2012: what happened and what's the MRM lesson?
flashcards.a: CIO swapped VaR methodology Jan 2012 without completed validation; spreadsheet copy-paste errors understated VaR (~$139M->~$80M region); limit breaches renegotiated; ~$6.2B loss, OCC $300M + Fed $200M + FCA £137.6M. Lesson: change control + shadow-running transitions + escalation integrity - a governance failure, not statistics.

flashcards.q: Barclays 2022 and Knight Capital 2012: what distinct risks do they illustrate?
flashcards.a: Barclays: override governance - unvalidated model overrides let it over-issue ~$15.2B structured notes (SEC $200M penalty). Knight: implementation/change risk - deployment flag error caused $440M loss in ~45 minutes. Validation doesn't cover deploy scripts; separate controls required.

flashcards.q: Typical tier-to-cadence mapping for model validation.
flashcards.a: Tier 1 (material/complex): full validation pre-use + annual revalidation + quarterly monitoring. Tier 2: every 2-3 years, semiannual monitoring. Tier 3: simplified initial review + periodic attestation + event-driven re-review. Re-tier when use expands.

flashcards.q: PSI thresholds and what they measure.
flashcards.a: Population Stability Index between development and current populations: <0.10 stable, 0.10-0.25 watch/investigate, >0.25 action (redevelop/recalibrate). Rule-of-thumb bands used in monitoring dashboards and challenger gating.

flashcards.q: List the promotion gates for a challenger model.
flashcards.a: Identical population/time windows in shadow mode; statistically significant improvement on decision metric (paired bootstrap on AUC/KS lift); no guardrail degradation (fairness ratios, tails); >=1 full seasonal cycle; rollback plan + revert trigger; governance approval logged as change ticket.

flashcards.q: How do you validate a black-box vendor scorecard?
flashcards.a: Outcome-level empirical testing on YOUR population: discrimination/calibration by segment, stability, benchmark vs incumbent, sensitivity to missing inputs, override analysis; contractual audit rights + SOC reports per 2023 interagency third-party guidance; document limitations as conditions of approval.

flashcards.q: Map LLM artifacts onto SR 11-7 concepts.
flashcards.a: Eval suites/golden datasets = outcomes-analysis evidence; CI/CD regression gates = automated backtesting at promotion time; model cards + prompt versioning = documentation; red-team exercises = effective challenge; hallucination incidents = model-risk events logged with severity/trends; human oversight thresholds for irreversible actions.

flashcards.q: NIST AI RMF functions mapped to SR 11-7?
flashcards.a: GOVERN -> policy/board reporting; MAP -> inventory/tiering/business context; MEASURE -> conceptual soundness + outcomes testing + monitoring metrics; MANAGE -> compensating controls, limitations register, incident response. GenAI Profile (July 2024) adds confabulation/information-integrity categories into MEASURE/MANAGE.

flashcards.q: Why is 'the model was fine, users misused it' not a defense?
flashcards.a: SR 11-7 defines model risk as including misuse: approved-use boundaries are part of the validation deliverable, enforced via API gating, usage logging, training, and monitoring that flags out-of-scope use. Governance failed even if the math was right.
